section.title: 10. Feature and backend characterization (M-05-A.2 accepted)

p.M05A2-SYNTAX: Characterize existing behavior, without introducing activation semantics. Core preserves feature activation strings and qualified requires keys. Resolver dep:group/name preserves the coordinate, but group/name/feature and group/name?/feature split at the first slash: runtime-confirmed parsing defect in the eight-case resolver family. Unqualified weak forwarding records a weak request without activating the dependency; qualified weak forwarding is misclassified as strong. Dependency inline features/optional fields are unsupported by the current wire schema.

p.M05A2-CONSTRAINTS: Legacy exclusive means at-most-one: zero and one members are valid, two fail. All-features is an activation request, not definition validity. validate_features_table currently reports an exclusive violation for an otherwise valid alternatives table: runtime-confirmed validation defect. requires_any remains technical OR, never a user selection policy or exactly-one group; multiple alternatives may coexist.

p.M05A2-BACKEND-MATRIX: Direct Rust routes: NaiveDepSolver::new(P: DepProvider).solve selects provider versions without backtracking. SatDepSolver::new(P: DepProvider).solve retries version bounds through NaiveDepSolver; it does not search disjunction alternatives. ResolvoDepSolver::new(P: VersionEnumerator).solve calls solve_hard with VibevmResolvoProvider, encodes requires_any as native union, then tries recommendations through further hard solves. The eight-case resolver family confirms that naive/SAT fail when the first OR alternative is absent despite an available second, and accept an already chosen alternative name at the wrong version; resolvo selects the available alternative and rejects the wrong-version case. All three permit both OR alternatives concurrently. Direct solve accepts roots only: default features and conditional targets are omitted, as the runtime control demonstrates; explicitly submitted incompatible version roots fail. This direct-entry limitation does not imply omission by install orchestration. No backend-switching fallback occurs in these entry routes. Actual production selection is source-audited through PackageSourceOptions, builder.rs, source.rs and cells.rs. validate_solver accepts None/resolvo/naive/sat and rejects unknown names. selection_flags maps None to resolvo. dep_solver has all nine explicit combinations of three backends with LocalRegistryDepProvider, MultiRegistryDepProvider, or EmbeddedDepProvider over LocalCompositeDepProvider and optional declared Multi provider. Invalid internal flag/resource combinations panic via unreachable, rather than choosing another backend. RegistryPackageSource delegates solve, manifest_of and solve_masked to its InstallResolver. PinnedLocalFactory builds explicit Local with default solver (resolvo), requires offline/no previous lock/no embedded root, and wraps an exact-pin qualifier. These are existing caller routes, not a new authority.

tr.td: First alternative or already chosen name; version-check gap
Inherits naive limitation; no alternative search

Explicit registry selects Local; otherwise discovered project-local/embedded roots select Embedded with optional declared walk; otherwise available declared/git/offline-store source selects Multi, or construction errors. All preserve validated solver override.
cell_selection → selection_flags → dep_solver → selected backend.solve(roots). All three backends supported for each provider; no automatic backend switch.

solve_masked_cell passes the same selected solver name and provider to vibe_install::solve_with_visibility_mask; metadata_manifest_cell uses the matching provider. The helper implementations are outside this read roster; no deeper masked-backend guarantee is inferred.
Qualified wrapper delegates substrate calls unchanged; pinned factory constructs Local/resolvo through the same builder and restricts qualification to its bound exact pin.

Calls source.solve, may retry with unheld roots through the same source after held-pin failure, then calls resolve_effective, fetch_or_defer with request.features, and expand_conditional_deps. Root retry is not solver fallback. Activation occurs outside the direct DepSolver API.

section.p: Weak-forwarding inventory: runtime tests confirm unqualified dep?/feature records weak_dep_features without activating the dependency; strong dep/feature activates it. Qualified group/name?/feature is incorrectly split into the strong map under group. features.rs merges weak maps independently, without applying them to another package. plan.rs passes FeatureRequest into fetch_or_defer and expand_conditional_deps, imported from its fetch child module. The literal read roster grants plan.rs, not crates/vibe-install/src/plan/fetch.rs; end-to-end weak-request consumption and conditional-loop retention are therefore not verified. This is a bounded evidence limitation, not a claim of missing production forwarding or convergence. Package-source selection and delegation are source-audited; no package-source integration tests were executed in this retry.

p.M05A2-CONDITIONAL: A name-present predicate is not a version constraint. ConditionalPredicate evaluates exact context tags and supports boolean not/and/or; richer probe assignments return Unsupported. Direct solvers omit target dependencies. Explicitly submitting a fired dependency constraint must enforce its version even if the name already exists. Separately, naive/SAT requires_any accepts an already chosen name without checking the alternative version (runtime-confirmed defect); resolvo enforces the alternative version. A negated self-trigger changes true to false when its dependency is added, so growth of requirements alone cannot prove final predicate consistency. Repros assert concrete before/after predicates and version outcomes, never a magic iteration count. Production conditional-loop retention or convergence defects remain hypotheses until that caller is exercised; this task does not change its semantics.

p.M05A2-REVIEW-BOUNDARY: These anchors and the m_05_a_2_cases library families were independently reviewed and accepted through Zap WorkAccepted revision 178; durable evidence is campaigns/next/evidence/M-05-A.2. Tests pin current behavior, not corrected behavior. Retry2 ran cargo test --offline --locked -p vibe-resolver --lib m_05_a_2_cases on the designated warm target: exit 0, eight passed, zero failed, 91 filtered out. The prior core run is reused unchanged: four passed, zero failed, 615 filtered out; SHA-256 confirms the retained core owner/test bytes are unchanged. No dependencies were downloaded by this task. Caller selection claims above are source observations, distinguished from the executed direct resolver tests. This acceptance covers the characterization only; solver replacement, activation fixes and conditional-loop convergence remain separate work.

p.M05B1-DECLARATIONS: A dependency declaration has a stable, package-local ID independent of ordering, version and option aliases. Legacy requires coordinates lower to kind-free group/name IDs. One declaration owns its source/version and explicit link/access/friend/exclude metadata. Local aliases resolve only in the declaring package and cannot shadow another ID. Duplicate IDs, ambiguous aliases and dangling metadata refuse normalization.

p.M05B1-EFFECTS: One typed algebra contains local feature references, dependency activation, strong and weak target-feature requests, exported subskill activation and declared config-value activation. Effects carry references, never duplicate dependency metadata. Strong forwarding activates its dependency; weak forwarding stays pending until that dependency is active, including activation supplied by the caller or a later merged expansion. Required declarations are active without optional activation. Config effects select declared values; conflicting values refuse expansion. No choices.requires engine is introduced.

p.M05B1-LOWERING: Legacy activation strings lower through the same algebra and expansion engine. Forwarding splits at the final slash, accepting local aliases or qualified group/name dependency references and one local target feature. Empty segments, extra slashes, misplaced question marks, version-bearing refs and invalid paths refuse. Full declaration-aware lowering validates every effect, including dormant private features, against dependencies, local features, exported subskills and config declarations. The historical table-only API has no declaration context: it checks syntax and local feature references but cannot establish dependency or export existence. It is a compatibility projection, not declaration validation. Definition validation does not activate all exclusive alternatives; default activation retains the legacy at-most-one check.

p.M05B1-SAFE-STOP: The normalized Rust API is available for typed construction and declaration-aware legacy lowering. New authored grammar, schema publication, constrained groups/domains and migration remain outside B1. Keep new grammar unpublished until lowering and validation agree. Cross-package installation integration and acceptance remain owner-controlled; this contract makes no claim of delivery to another package.

p.M05B1-CHARACTERIZATION-SUPERSESSION: M05A2-SYNTAX and M05A2-CONSTRAINTS retain their accepted historical observations and receipts. B1 supersedes only their first-slash forwarding and definition-validation defect assertions: qualified forwarding now separates the final local feature, preserves group/name, and recognizes weak requests; validating definitions does not select exclusive alternatives. The two existing live test names are retained as corrected regressions. All other M05A2 laws and evidence remain unchanged, including at-most-one activation and requires_any technical OR.

p.M05B1-MANIFEST-CALLERS: Full-manifest install fetch/defer and configuration preview normalize requires declarations and compose declaration-aware lowering with the shared evaluator. Legacy requires declarations are required (the wire has no optional field); required dependencies seed weak forwarding. Undeclared default activations and dormant references refuse before a feature expansion is returned. Available exports are declaration context, never inferred from feature uses. A full legacy Manifest has no authoritative exported-subskill catalogue: unavailable is distinct from a known empty catalogue. Its dependency-aware lowering validates all known dependencies and local references, while retaining well-formed legacy subskill selectors for incumbent downstream validation. Returned selectors do not prove export existence. Fully declared typed and legacy entrypoints still validate every export against their supplied catalogue. The table-only API remains for callers genuinely lacking declarations. This boundary does not publish new grammar or claim cross-package request delivery.

p.M05B2-GROUPS: Constrained groups declare zero-or-more, one-or-more, zero-or-one or exactly-one cardinality and package-local feature members. Positive member and group guards are explicit references in an acyclic guard dependency graph; unknown, dangling, foreign-package and expression guards refuse even in dormant definitions. Ordinary feature-effect cycles retain B1 semantics. Group membership is unambiguous. Defaults, when declared, must satisfy the declared membership and cardinality. This normalized API does not publish new TOML features/requires grammar or a choices.requires engine; requires_any remains a technical disjunction.

p.M05B2-CONSUMERS: Consumer configuration request/result epoch 1 retain each consumer and DependencyDeclarationId, DependencyRole, owner-qualified DefinitionId and TargetInstanceId, explicit selected LockTargetRole, resolution-domain identity and instance/configuration identity. LockId is optional before locking; absence never fabricates an established lock. Admitted source definitions are caller inputs, never filesystem or installed-world lookup. Unification is within one explicit domain/instance, not global package name. A reused instance cannot silently change package or configuration identity. Separate environment domains may select different configurations. Native backend version identities are opaque bytes represented as strings, never converted through Vibe SemVer; existing Vibe PackageRef versions keep their semantics.

p.M05B2-SELECTION: Omitted selection and explicit empty selection remain distinct. Additive requests union within a shared instance. Exact requests must agree; additive requests must fit every exact selection. Conflict results identify both original consumer edges. Declared defaults apply only to omitted selections under explicit consumer UseDeclaredDefaults policy, with provenance retained; they are not solver preferences and never replace an explicit selection. Inactive branch requests remain in result provenance without activating their members. All-features and ordinary feature closure cannot implicitly select constrained members. Active unresolved required groups return NeedsSelection with no feature effects or writes.

p.M05B2-COMPOSITION: The public pure consumer resolver admits the actual generated request beside its wire shape, validates constrained definitions, combines explicit consumer selections and composes the existing FeatureProgram/FeatureDeclarations evaluator. Resolved output includes the full existing feature expansion. Definition discovery and NeedsSelection perform no I/O. Legacy defaults, exclusive groups, weak forwarding and unavailable versus known-empty exports retain the B1 API behavior. Authored migration, cross-package installation delivery, lock persistence and acceptance remain separate owner-controlled work.

p.M05B3-PROFILES: The immutable source profiles features-legacy-absent-r1 and features-legacy-epoch1-r1 use the existing string-array FeaturesTable grammar. Their respective targets are features-typed-absent-r1 and features-typed-epoch1-r1, selected only explicitly. Recipes features-to-typed-r1 and features-to-typed-epoch1-r1 connect only their matching cohorts; identity-r1 connects each typed target to itself. The absent cohort forbids package.epoch; the epoch1 cohort requires integer 1 and preserves its exact token. Unknown profiles and epochs refuse. Ordinary Manifest::parse_str and all materialization/boot-source profiles retain their existing grammar and identities.

p.M05B3-GRAMMAR: Both cohorts admit a finite package document: root package, requires, requires_any and features only. Package requires string name/group/kind/version, kind flow/feat/stack/tool/mcp/lang; optional strings description/license/homepage/materialization, optional string arrays authors/keywords, optional booleans bridge/frozen, and only the cohort's epoch marker. Materialization is absent or copy/hardlink/in-place. Requires retains its existing packages and capabilities fields. Package entries retain qualified source coordinates, version (string or version.var), path/git/tag/branch/rev/auth/token_env/link/access/friend/exclude, interpreted by the existing Requires owner. Capabilities is a string array; version.var is a single string; friend is boolean and exclude is a string array. Link is static/dynamic/static-transitive/static-hard; access is public/private/friends-only; auth is none/token-env/credential-helper/ssh. Other dependency fields are strings. Legacy features/optional options are recognized only as unresolved input, never discarded or admitted by the target. requires_any is an array of tables with exactly one_of, an array of package-reference strings, and retains its technical-OR meaning and is never a constrained user-choice group. Normal and inline tables have the same meaning. Every other field or primitive shape refuses this revision.

p.M05B3-TYPED-SPELLING: In the typed targets, each features key other than exclusive is an array of closed effect tables: { local = "name" }, { dependency = "group/name" }, or { dependency = "group/name", feature = "name", strength = "strong" } (strength may instead be weak). No other keys or implicit strength are admitted. Each features.exclusive entry is { cardinality = "zero-or-one", members = ["name", ...] }; its members preserve their source order and its constraints compose the actual B2 Constraints model. The target reader returns actual B1 FeatureDeclarations and FeatureProgram together with B2 Constraints and Selection::Omitted. It retains the complete validated manifest meaning, including canonical legacy feature projection, rather than validating a stripped or dummy manifest. Dependencies remain required and own all source/version/link/access/friend/exclude metadata once. The default feature remains an explicit feature definition; absent default or consumer selection is not synthesized. No consumer policy, explicit-empty request, or UseDeclaredDefaults adoption is invented.

p.M05B3-AMBIGUITY: Dependency aliases are resolved only from the captured requires declarations: an unqualified dependency name denotes its unique declared coordinate; colliding names and duplicate normalized dependency declarations require input. Forwarding splits at the final slash using the B1 lowering law, and strong/weak distinction survives. A missing or ambiguous dependency/local-feature interpretation, slash-bearing feature/group name, empty, unknown, overlapping or private constrained membership, unsupported option, or subskill/config reference without an authoritative catalogue produces structured NeedsInput identifying the authored reference and finite corrective choices before any planned edits are returned. Source-media and resource-path fields are not reused. This revision promises no answer API: the caller edits the source and makes a fresh plan. No LLM or ambient resolver supplies mappings.

p.M05B3-PRESERVATION: Migration uses ordered provable token edits through the incumbent planner. Replace individual activation string tokens with their typed effect tables; wrap exclusive member arrays without changing their elements or internal comments. Copy every byte outside those spans, including unrelated values, dependency metadata, comments, order and quote style. Validate the result with the explicitly selected target reader. Deterministic replanning and typed-target identity are byte-identical. Dry-run has no authored effects; workspace saved-state application and recovery use the same selected reader and existing intent/before-image/barrier/approved-byte qualification. Neither hostile OS writer exclusion nor a new publication engine is claimed.

p.M05C1-IDENTITY: Candidate identity binds its exact selected source, content and definition, in addition to its package coordinate and version. A version alone, a label, an invented cache hit or a substituted definition cannot establish identity. Catalog inspection exposes reproducible evidence of the actual admitted definitions and source/content bindings.

p.M05C1-TRANSACTION: One resolution transaction reads one immutable candidate catalog. Capability discovery, candidate dependency reads and selected-manifest observation use the same captured definitions; repeated access cannot reopen mutable same-version metadata. Candidate capability discovery is pure and cannot activate a discarded candidate or request global consumer selection. Consumer configuration retains the incumbent B1/B2/B3 semantics.

p.M05C1-FAILURE: Unavailable or corrupt catalog data is a source failure, distinct from a valid candidate lacking a requested option. Source failure stops before install effects and is not converted to incompatibility, fallback selection, or another definition. Existing published source absence and source precedence rules remain intact.

p.M05C1-OBSERVATION: ETO observes the actual reproducible catalog identity and its inspected candidate bindings before install effects. This transaction consistency does not declare candidate-conditioned activation or universal route parity complete; those remain subsequent work.

p.M05C2-CONDITIONING: Activation belongs to the exact candidate that introduced it. The existing resolvo solver must carry induced requirements on that candidate's literal. Already-authorized ordinary-feature implications remain candidate-local solver requirements while a group is unresolved; unresolved choices neither erase known requirements nor authorize guessed members. B2 continues to expose no full expansion for NeedsSelection. Rejecting a candidate discards its features, providers, dependency effects, subskills and config values. Only selected candidates contribute returned effects; inspecting an unreachable candidate with a mandatory unresolved group never requests selection.

p.M05C2-CONSUMERS: Every original incoming consumer edge, selection intent, version constraint and provenance survives candidate rejection unchanged. Evaluate all consumers of one configuration together through the B2 evaluator. A valid older candidate may satisfy the same authorized intent. Conflict evidence retains original consumer reasons alongside the candidate coordinate and exact C1 identity; source errors remain operational errors, never candidate exclusions.

p.M05C2-DEFAULTS: Permission to use a declared default binds the exact shown candidate source/content/definition identity. Choosing another definition does not authorize its defaults, even if it is older or the member spelling happens to match. A selected candidate without that exact binding requires rediscovery before effects are returned. The comparison covers default-governed omitted intent even when the current definition removes the shown default or group and therefore reports no defaults used. Explicit selections retain their original meaning and are not replaced by defaults.

p.M05C2-BOUNDARY: The configured resolver consumes admitted, source-bound B1/B2 definitions and immutable C1 metadata. Unsupported combinations refuse before returning mutation effects. Completeness is the existing solver's finite candidate search, never a fixed retry limit. Legacy DepSolver routes, ordinary manifest parsing, B3 opt-in profiles and C1 operational-error propagation remain intact; universal caller-route parity is separate C3 work. Counterexamples compare the entire selected graph and all derived effects, including provider contributions.

p.M05C2-ADMITTED-SURFACE: The configured Rust entry accepts fixed explicit incoming Vibe consumer requests, one configuration instance per package, and normalized definitions supplied by the admitting caller with exact C1 receipts. It preserves the full request rather than inferring edges from installed state. Default authorization retains that request and the full shown normalized definition as well as its source/content/definition receipt. Native candidate selection, multiple instances of one package, cross-package feature forwarding and non-registry dependency sources refuse. Conditional targets and obsoletes refuse on this entry because their complete activation support remains unavailable. C3 admits technical disjunctions through the incumbent solver with selected declaration/provider witnesses retained; no first-alternative inference supplies their edges. These refusals are explicit unsupported outcomes, not unsatisfiability claims or a substitute resolver. The ordinary resolver routes and B1/B2 standalone APIs retain their existing semantics.

p.M05C3-REQUEST: Every supported solve, metadata, masked, conditional and visibility route consumes the same immutable normalized request and candidate catalog. Preserve every incoming root constraint and consumer intent, including repeated coordinates, exact selections and candidate-bound default permission. Route-specific masks and additional conditional requirements never replace or weaken the original request. Metadata must expose the selected candidate's requested effects rather than reconstructing an older unconfigured manifest.

p.M05C3-ROOT-UNION: Bare install preserves every workspace member declaration and its constraint origin. Explicit CLI install/update preserves every supplied CLI root, superseding a named coordinate's old declaration only on the exact selected project node being edited. Other members' original constraints remain active; for CLI-named coordinates their ranges are not converted to old lock pins. Unnamed coordinates retain minimum-churn hold-pins behavior. Incompatible active constraints produce a typed conflict with origins, never first-wins loss. Plans retain normalized intent and selected declaration/provider provenance through the confirmation boundary.

p.M05C3-EDGES: The final graph retains the actual selected dependency edges, including capability providers and technical disjunction alternatives. Each edge carries its selected declaration and provider provenance. A set of all possible providers, the first authored alternative, or an inference from coincidental package presence is not evidence of the solver's selected edge. Visibility retry preserves consumer requests and exact choices on retained edges.

p.M05C3-REFUSAL: A backend unable to honor a requested capability returns a typed refusal retaining the selected backend; it never falls back to another backend. Ordinary supported disjunction and capability routes must retain their choices rather than being blanket-refused. Genuinely incomplete conditional/configuration combinations remain explicitly unsupported. A bounded retry does not establish complete conditional solving. Never apply a graph assembled from inconsistent routes.

p.M05C3-ADMISSION: The existing Rust source seam may bind explicitly admitted consumer requests, candidate definitions and exact default receipts to the immutable catalog and forward them through the existing planner. Legacy roots and FeatureRequest flags remain lossless legacy intent; they do not authorize fabricated B2 identities. New CLI, authored grammar, schema and persistence are outside this admission. Configured OR routes may use the retained solver witnesses; incomplete conditional/configuration combinations still refuse explicitly.

p.M05C3-PARITY: Fixtures exercise the actual production source and planner forwarding paths. Supported routes produce identical selected graphs with selected declaration/provider provenance, or equivalent typed conflicts. Structural inspection alone does not establish semantic acceptance. This contract preserves the C1 immutable catalog and C2 candidate-conditioned semantics, defaults and known implications; it does not publish new authored grammar or infer normalized consumer identities from installed state.

p.M05D1-REQUEST: A production lock records the normalized authored request and its digest separately from resolved active and dormant selections and feature closure. Root constraints retain their consumer and declaration origins. Explicit empty selections, omitted selections, selection intent, domain, target and exact default authorization remain distinct. Derived selections are never the sole authored authority.

p.M05D1-IDENTITY: Each selected technical dependency or capability provider edge records the exact source declaration, consumer intent, owner source capture, content and definition identity, and selected provider identity. Reuse C1 receipts, C3 selected witnesses and B1/B2 evaluation. Exact replay rejects changed same-version definitions, missing request digests, missing authored authority and changed default receipts; it never infers default authorization from prior outcomes.

p.M05D1-READER: The actual apply path writes this record and the normal planner reads and validates it. Legacy locks remain recognizable as derived state eligible for intentional regeneration under PROP-044. The registry lockfile epoch and core schema version are independent of the configuration-record epoch. Unknown configuration epochs refuse without silently regenerating or reinterpreting them. Generated schema and ordering machinery remain the wire authority. This addition does not change solver semantics, global discovery, authored grammar or the core-to-wire dependency direction.

p.M05D1-INVOCATION: For a current configured lock, bare-install exact reuse requires current authoritative normalized intent and explicit default receipts from the existing admitted source seam, with matching captures and definitions. Legitimately retained authored decision receipts suffice; repeated human permission is not required. Missing current authority refuses and never strips configuration. Explicit CLI roots permit fresh resolution of named coordinates under current authority, not dropping other configuration, changing other choices or inferring new default permission. InstallRequest.exact remains manifest pinning. Full exact-reinstall/update routing and prompt-free prepared offline reinstall remain E.2; D1 adds no CLI flag.

p.M05D2-LOADING-COMPOSITION: Install passes its current preflight configuration record explicitly through ordinary and native boot composition before durable lock publication. Durable regeneration and analysis read the published record. The workspace owner joins each exact package coordinate and content identity to selected exports and validates the captured child declarations through the admitted slot. Eager content enters the node dependency loading lane. Lazy-push uses that lane's existing dynamic INDEX offer: its description, captured declaration reference and read_subskill request reach agent context; the agent requests content when relevant through MCP. Lazy-pull is listed by query_package and delivered only through read_subskill. This connection does not introduce a task-matching engine or another agent launcher. For this derived-view path, full-slot materialization supersedes the historical eager/project-tree and lazy/cache copy descriptions in section 2.5.0; materialise_subskill reports the already materialized slot without copying into the project tree. Legacy lock readers retain their previous compatibility semantics.

p.M05D2-DORMANT: Dormant selections remain authored intent. Validate requested groups and members against the current exact admitted definition before evaluating guards: a removed dormant option diagnoses drift, even while its branch is inactive. An inactive branch emits no feature, subskill or config effects. Reactivation uses the retained authored selection, never a derived selection promoted to authority or an invented default. This preserves M05B2-SELECTION and M05D1-REQUEST.

p.M05D2-CONSUMER-BOUNDARY: Selected exports must reach real visibility, loading and package projection consumers with declaration identity, delivery mode and provider provenance intact. Full captured and materialized package content and its content identity remain independent of activation; only effective contributions and target projection may change. Do not admit completed subskill semantics until every required consumer works. Export-to-consumer mappings require authoritative declarations, never inference from directory presence. This requirement does not publish new authored grammar or weaken exact request, definition and default receipts.

p.M05D2-CAPTURED-DECLARATIONS: The subskill export catalogue consists of actual SubskillManifest declarations from the exact admitted captured provider. Canonical subskill.path, content.files_written, delivery, description and activation belong to that declaration; validate its path and content membership against the capture and retain provider, capture and definition provenance. A directory or a selector alone is not an export. Independent [[skill]] and extension declarations retain their existing semantics; no relation to a subskill is inferred from names, paths or presence.

p.M05D2-DELIVERY-CONSUMERS: A derived contribution view joins B1/B2 selected exports and D1 exact requested/resolved selections to captured child declarations. Selected eager content participates in ordinary workspace loading. Selected lazy-pull content is discoverable and read from the admitted captured slot only on request. Selected lazy-push content reaches the actual context-offer/delivery mechanism with its description and content reference, without eager Agent Skill substitution or project-file writes. Every required consumer must work before subskill semantics are admitted; an unused helper or test-only publisher does not discharge this requirement.

p.M05D2-FULL-SLOTS: PROP-009 full-slot materialization remains intact, including unselected files. Activation changes effective loading and generated projection, never captured or materialized package bytes or content identity. Do not repopulate legacy subskills_active rows to restore install-time project-tree copying. The derived view may be recomputed from existing exact lock selections and captured declarations without a new lock epoch. M05B1 identity and declaration laws, M05B2 default and dormant-selection laws, and M05D1 authored-request and exact-replay laws remain unchanged.

section.title: Request freshness and pure cached discovery

p.M05E1-FRESHNESS: Before any bare-install or empty-root Fresh decision, compare current normalized request and definition/default receipts with the retained requested record, using the D1 codec and identity rather than a second fingerprint. Report the retained and current request identity in the decision. Missing current configured authority never permits Fresh. Legacy locks may reuse the historical default request only; nondefault feature intent requires resolution. This supersedes the M05A1-FRESH-REQUESTED-FEATURES bug characterization, not its historical evidence. D1 exact-replay refusals and all independent root, source, solver, epoch and acquisition laws remain intact.

p.M05E1-DISCOVERY: Discovery consumes only M16 frozen manifest resources through a shared Rust service. Return candidate resource/content identity and complete authored definitions, including effects, choices and declared defaults, without selecting a candidate or applying defaults, solving, invoking providers, fetching or writing authored/cache state. Empty prepared input is unavailable. Candidates needing consumer action return stable NeedsSelection; repeating the same unresolved input does not retry preparation. Purity counters describe operations performed by this service, not unobserved external activity. Explicit caller preparation remains separate. CLI and MCP use the same service; the legacy locked-feature view remains available. No discovery response admits an install or supplies default authorization.

p.M05E1-ADMITTED-CAPTURE: The normalized discovery input is an explicitly admitted immutable B2 CandidateConfiguration, its exact C1 CandidateMetadata receipt and the exact manifest bytes bound by the admitting owner to an M16 captured resource. Validate the resource, retained bytes, package/version, receipt and complete normalized constraints before projection; missing or substituted authority is unavailable. Reuse the D1 lossless definition projection, retaining instance/domain, guards, dormant alternatives, typed effects and declared defaults. A raw manifest digest is only a byte witness, never a replacement C1 content or definition receipt. Queries borrow a prepared basis and do not prepare again; adapters without that basis report unavailable. Explicit disk capture alone grants neither normalized authority nor default consent. These additive E1 rules preserve every B1/B2/C1/C2/C3/D1 law.

p.M05E1-CLI-HOST-QUERY: Ordinary CLI discovery may query an explicitly caller-trusted local M16 host endpoint using --discovery-host and --capture. The host retains PreparedConfigurationDiscovery created by typed B2/C1 admission; it checks the exact capture and root and returns only that immutable query projection. The endpoint is supplied by the trusted embedding host, not discovered from package files. This is a presentation transport, not admission of a serialized definition or authentication by a DTO flag. The CLI does not construct normalized authority from the response, persist it, or use it for install. No endpoint starts a host or prepares resources implicitly; raw-only invocation remains unavailable. Host preparation and endpoint lifecycle remain caller-owned.

p.M05E2-EXACT-REINSTALL: Prepared exact reinstall consumes the retained D1 authored request and resolved lock, current authoritative decision/default receipts and the exact captured source/content/definition identities for every locked package, including packages with no dependency edges. It validates their agreement before continuation, lifecycle or materialization effects. It replays locked selections and payloads without solving, choosing defaults or preparing a replacement capture. Missing captures, changed definitions or inconsistent payloads return an explicit unavailable/stale result before effects. A fully prepared offline replay requires no selection or confirmation prompt. The ordinary unprepared route must not claim this prepared guarantee.

p.M05E2-UPDATE-INTENT: Update retains original authored consumer requests, explicit empty selections and dormant selections, rather than promoting resolved choices to authored authority. A changed package default cannot replace an explicit selection. Removed selected members or groups and new required groups require explicit reconfiguration; the solver cannot select their replacement or newly required option. Omitted intent governed by declared defaults still requires exact shown-definition authorization under M05C2-DEFAULTS. A changed definition does not inherit consent from its predecessor. Evaluate retained intent through the existing B1/B2 engine and use the incumbent selected resolver for technical dependency solving; introduce no second selection engine.

p.M05E2-REPORT: Replay/update decisions distinguish exact reuse, semantic input change, unavailable evidence and reconfiguration required. Report retained and current authored request identity and exact before/after definition, source/payload and induced graph/effect differences, including selected declaration/provider provenance and dormant selections. Missing evidence is unavailable, never an empty difference or exact reuse. A reconfiguration result retains every actionable removed selection, required group and default-authorization gap and applies no drift. A proposed candidate or a report alone is not permission to apply it.

p.M05E2-FORCE-AND-CONFIRMATION: Reinstall force remains materialization repair of the same exact locked bytes and branch; it cannot authorize changed definitions, substitute captures, select another option or force a lifecycle repark. Assume-yes answers an existing apply confirmation only; it never supplies a selection or new default authorization. Preserve ordinary legacy command, source, lifecycle, epoch and confirmation laws outside the explicitly prepared exact route. These E2 rules refine reinstall/update invocation and reporting; they do not replace B1/B2 evaluation, C1 capture identity, C2 default consent, C3 root/provenance retention, D1 persistence or D2 full-slot and contribution laws.

p.M05E2-EXPOSURE: Functional exposure requires a positive fixture driven through each claimed real non-test entrypoint and its standard source constructor, including prepared inputs. Proposed helpers, direct helper fixtures, parsing and serialization do not establish command or orchestration exposure. The m_05_e_2_cases test families and their exact nonzero selections must be created and bound to their owning Cargo targets before dispatch. Specification status here records requirements only, not implementation, validation or acceptance.

p.M05E3-PREFLIGHT: Before product writes, retain the complete desired graph, authored request and immutable catalog preconditions, trust/collision/loading/effect validation and exact before-images. Unsat, NeedsSelection, unavailable authority or catalog/request drift refuse before writes. Root-union planning and exact/default/dormant/empty intent remain governed by B1/B2/C1/C2/C3/D1/D2/E1/E2; this section replaces no independent law.

p.M05E3-RECOVERY: Coordinate manifest, lock, owned-slot and boot prefixes with durable before-images and write-ahead phase intent. The existing role-restricted boot journal remains the boot publication owner; manifest and slot paths never masquerade as boot roles. Interrupted or failed work retains recovery state. Recovery refuses an unproved or third state rather than overwriting it. Local byte restoration is not full rollback when a hook, agent, in-place update or other external effect may have run. Retain that uncertainty even after local restoration.

p.M05E3-REMOVAL: Plan removal from the complete workspace declarations and selected dependency edges before deletion. Distinguish the selected node's explicit declaration, other members' roots and shared transitive dependencies. Explain reverse dependents and the desired keep/remove closure before confirmation. Never prune an incomplete graph, an unknown footprint or unowned user state. Preserve in-place destructive confirmation and adoption-facts ownership.

p.M05E3-ADMITTED-RECONFIGURATION: An explicit reconfiguration or prepared configured removal consumes a new caller-admitted authored request, the complete workspace root union and exact captured catalog through the incumbent planner. This explicit invocation may replace the selected authored configuration; ordinary update, bare install and exact replay continue to require their retained intent. No assume-yes, changed default, derived lock choice or discovery projection supplies this authority. Missing selections refuse before product writes. The distinction is invocation authority, not a second evaluator or resolver.

p.M05E3-RECOVERY-IDENTITY: Deletion membership is immutable outside its planning owner. Before-image and footprint readers preserve native filename identity or refuse unsupported names before mutation; lossy UTF-8 decoding and backslash-to-slash normalization cannot authorize deletion. Recovery reopens only an explicitly selected operation with the original admitted target set, validates retained image structure and refuses third states before any restoration. An interrupted local restore may resume only from proved before/checkpoint file states. Changed node boot requires compensation through its own publication owner; a local-prefix-only restore is incomplete recovery and retains its evidence and external-effect uncertainty. Flagged nonfatal post-install hook failure also retains evidence.

p.M05E3-EXPOSURE: Failure injection must cover manifest, slot, boot and lock boundaries with retained recovery evidence, and hooks must not imply unproved rollback. Positive fixtures drive each claimed ordinary install/orchestration/uninstall entrypoint and its standard prepared source. A helper fixture, proposed test family or specification anchor alone establishes neither production exposure nor acceptance.
